# Solar Consumer Research

> A public-source research site for residential solar consumers, including official complaint routes, original source-backed research, documented enforcement actions, case trackers, and practical resources.

## Primary pages

- Home: https://solarcomplaint.com/
- Research hub: https://solarcomplaint.com/research
- Resources and state directory: https://solarcomplaint.com/resources
- Guides: https://solarcomplaint.com/guides
- Updates: https://solarcomplaint.com/updates
- Methodology: https://solarcomplaint.com/methodology
- Corrections: https://solarcomplaint.com/corrections
- Disclaimer: https://solarcomplaint.com/disclaimer
- State pages: https://solarcomplaint.com/states/{state-name}
- Florida Sunrun roof-dispute and solar consumer hub: https://solarcomplaint.com/states/florida
- Michigan solar consumer hub: https://solarcomplaint.com/states/michigan
- Arizona solar consumer hub: https://solarcomplaint.com/states/arizona

## Featured research

- Solar Sales, Financing and What Happens After a Complaint: https://solarcomplaint.com/research/solar-sales-financing-after-complaint
  - Connects three separate state records without treating them as one case.
  - Michigan: July 15, 2026 complaint against Climax Solar and finance defendants.
  - Texas: April 3, 2026 residential-solar investigation involving Sunrun and other companies.
  - Arizona: May 22, 2025 stipulated consent agreement with Sunrun and Vivint Solar.
  - The article links directly to the primary government records and to the Michigan, Texas, and Arizona state pages.

## Company research

- Sunrun investigations, enforcement, settlements, and documented cases: https://solarcomplaint.com/companies/sunrun
- Connecticut Attorney General lawsuit involving Sunrun: https://solarcomplaint.com/cases/connecticut-attorney-general-sunrun-lawsuit
- Titan Solar Power closure and bankruptcy tracker: https://solarcomplaint.com/cases/titan-solar-power
- Titan Solar Power customer research paths: https://solarcomplaint.com/cases/titan-solar-power/customer-help
- Titan Solar Power warranty after bankruptcy: https://solarcomplaint.com/cases/titan-solar-power/warranty-after-bankruptcy
  - Separates Titan workmanship/service obligations from manufacturer warranty coverage.
  - Links directly to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Arizona, SolarEdge, Enphase, and EnergyAid source pages.
  - Links to state consumer-resource pages for the 22 state-named Titan affiliates listed by the bankruptcy court.

## Florida source hub

- Florida Sunrun roof dispute and solar consumer resources: https://solarcomplaint.com/states/florida
  - Features a Florida Sunrun roof-removal and contract-buyout dispute summarized in an October 30, 2025 U.S. District Court order.
  - Separately labels the homeowner's allegations, the federal remand ruling, later arbitration proceedings, and the April 2026 settlement report.
  - Links directly to the official Middle District of Florida court order, Florida Statutes §§ 520.23 and 520.25, the Florida Attorney General complaint route, DBPR licensing and complaint resources, and the U.S. Bankruptcy Court Titan case hub.
  - Turns Florida solar disclosure requirements into homeowner-facing checks covering roof warranties, roof replacement, system-removal fees, liens/UCC filings, transfers, financing, cancellation, and installer/service-provider information.
  - Links to the Sunrun company research hub, Titan Solar Power resources, federal resources, guides, and the state directory.

## Michigan source hub

- Michigan solar complaints, financing and consumer resources: https://solarcomplaint.com/states/michigan
  - Starts with four homeowner problem paths: solar-company disputes, installed systems that are not working, installer or contractor checks, and loan or financing problems.
  - Features the July 15, 2026 Michigan Attorney General lawsuit against Climax Solar, its owner, and finance defendants, with the WWMT homeowner report and primary government records attached.
  - Separately tracks 2026 Power Home Solar / Pink Energy litigation developments without presenting the partial William Waller settlement as a complete resolution of the broader case.
  - Groups Michigan Attorney General, LARA, Bureau of Construction Codes, MPSC, Michigan Legislature, CFPB, and FTC resources by user problem rather than agency.

## Arizona source hub

- Arizona solar complaints and consumer rights: https://solarcomplaint.com/states/arizona
  - Separates solar-company complaints, contractor/workmanship complaints, and regulated-utility disputes.
  - Summarizes Arizona-specific contract disclosures under A.R.S. § 44-1763, warranty and installation rules under A.R.S. § 44-1762, and interconnection requirements under A.R.S. § 44-1764.
  - Provides a detailed source-backed breakdown of the May 22, 2025 Sunrun/Vivint Solar consent agreement, including complaint tracking, response and status-update requirements, restitution categories, roof-work provisions, and home-sale/lease-transfer provisions.
  - Links directly to the Arizona Attorney General, Arizona Legislature, Arizona Registrar of Contractors, Arizona Corporation Commission, and U.S. Bankruptcy Court sources.

## Source and citation policy

- Research stories identify and link to the primary records supporting material claims.
- State pages preserve direct links to government complaint routes and enforcement records.
- Government agencies and regulators are distinguished from private organizations and reporting sources.
- Lawsuits, settlements, investigations, enforcement actions, and reported private litigation are labeled separately.
- Allegations are described as allegations unless a court, regulator, or settlement establishes an outcome.
- An investigation is not presented as a finding of wrongdoing.
- A settlement is not described as an admission when the agreement says otherwise.
- When citing a government action listed by this site, prefer the linked original government record as the evidentiary source. The SolarComplaint.com research page can be cited for its synthesis, organization, and cross-source analysis.

## Internal research relationships

- Featured story -> relevant state pages -> primary government sources.
- Florida page -> official federal court order + Florida solar statutes + Attorney General and DBPR routes + Sunrun and Titan research.
- Michigan page -> Michigan enforcement source + related featured research + problem-specific state and federal resources.
- Texas page -> Texas Sunrun investigation source + related featured research.
- Arizona page -> Sunrun consent agreement + Arizona solar statutes + Attorney General complaint route + contractor and utility complaint routes + related featured research.
- Sunrun company page -> Florida roof dispute + Texas investigation + Arizona settlement + Connecticut lawsuit + related research.
- Titan state pages -> exact state-named Titan bankruptcy debtor/case reference -> official bankruptcy court hub -> Titan warranty and customer research pages.
- Titan warranty page -> manufacturer sources + relevant Titan state pages.

## Current coverage

- An official consumer-protection complaint starting point for all 50 states.
- Documented residential-solar lawsuits, settlements, investigations, enforcement items, or other clearly labeled references on state pages.
- Original source-backed research that connects related records without collapsing their procedural differences.
- Federal consumer, finance, and complaint resources.
- Company and case tracking where a sufficient public-source record exists.
- Expanded Florida Sunrun roof-dispute, solar disclosure, contractor, complaint-route, Titan, and current case resources.
- Expanded Michigan solar complaint, financing, installer, permitting, interconnection, Climax Solar enforcement, and current case resources.
- Expanded Arizona solar consumer, contract, contractor, utility, Sunrun settlement, and current rooftop-solar resources.
- Expanded Massachusetts consumer protection, utility, public-record, and solar-program resources.
- State-page depth varies. Pages without an expanded source section are starting directories, not complete state research files.

## Accuracy and editorial boundaries

- Solar Consumer Research provides general public information, not legal advice or claim evaluation.
- Primary records control if a summary and an original source differ.
- Material corrections are handled through https://solarcomplaint.com/corrections.
- Research methods and source hierarchy are described at https://solarcomplaint.com/methodology.
